about: CHAIN rollo_911 (Design/content/chains/rollo_911.md): the Seine in the hands of the Northmen, and Rollo made lord at Rotomagus in 911. Fourteen cards, 904 to 918 and after. A skipper's word on the Channel (s00) sends a boat up to a ruined market (s01); the archbishop's canon and the Northmen's steward both want her (s02 to s04); after the defeat before Chartres on 20 July 911 the player chooses whom to help (s05): the camp (road_peace), the archbishop (road_church) or Count Robert at Paris (road_franks). Then the meeting on the Epte (s06_epte) or the bridge at Pitres (s06_bridge), the baptism of 912 (s07), Rollo's law (s08), the relapsed converts and the letter to Reims (s09). Three endings: end_peace (what happened: a plot and a free keel in Rollo's Rouen), end_saint (what happened, on the church's side: Saint Ouen comes home in 918) and end_river_shut (history changed: no grant, the fleet leaves the Seine, flag changed_rollo_911_no_grant). Progress is flags ch_rollo_911_0 to _9; the timed flag ch_rollo_911_wait makes the waits real. Every card is drawn on a call at its port when its 'when' holds (weights 40 to 60), except the start (0.8). The forge names the people; the words call the invented ones Ketil, Gozbert, Odilard, Warin and Thorstein. Rollo, Count Robert, the archbishop of Rouen (Witto in Flodoard, Franco in Dudo: the cards never name him), Herve of Reims and King Charles are real. Words: Data/writing/chain_rollo_911.json; each option's note names the writing key of its outcome text. Sources in the notes and the chain page. Written 6 Oct 2026; a draft for the user to overwrite.

cards.note: Step 0, the hook: Quentovic, Parisius, Lundenwic or Hamwic, 904 to 910. A skipper says nobody sails to Rouen and that the three boats that do are paid well. Truth under it: Northmen held the lower Seine from the siege of Paris (885 to 886) on (Annales Vedastini 885; dossiers/rotomagus.md 5); armies buy food (realms/francia.md). The price words are ours. Sets ch_rollo_911_0. Refusing costs nothing; he tells it again another day.

cards.note: Step 1: Rotomagus, 904 to 910, on a call there. The town as the sources leave it: the wall of reused stone, the two cathedral churches joined, the saints carried inland, a toll place and a mint of 864 with nobody to use them (dossiers/rotomagus.md 1, 2, 6; Dudo 10 for 'poor men and ruined merchants'). The Northmen in Rouen with their whole army in 885 (Annales Vedastini). Ketil the steward (Old Norse Ketill), Gozbert the canon (Goz- + -bert) and Odilard the wine seller are invented; horses in the amphitheatre and the count of eleven canons are ours. Every option sets ch_rollo_911_1.

cards.note: Step 2: Rotomagus, a month or more after step 1, before 911. The archbishop (Witto, 889 to about 910, in the lists: dossiers/rotomagus.md 3) sends a letter to Count Robert at Paris. THE LETTER IS INVENTED; what is real is that the archbishops stayed in the city through the Northmen's years and were the go-betweens (Dudo 10 and 13, LATER), and that Robert, brother of King Odo, held Paris and the march against the Northmen (Wikipedia 'Robert I of France'). Sets ch_rollo_911_2; ch_rollo_911_letter if it is carried; ch_rollo_911_letter_shown if the steward hears it.

cards.note: Step 3, the first turn: Parisius, before 912. Warin (invented; an attested Frankish name), a man of Count Robert, asks what lies under the wall at Rouen. Real: Robert held the county of Paris after his brother Odo, who held the city in the siege of 885 to 886 (Abbo, Bella Parisiacae urbis; chronicle_793.json 885-11-24-siege-paris). Paris is one of the ten mints of 864 (Edict of Pitres c. 12). Turn payout: 100 d for the truth (ch_rollo_911_told_franks), or a doubtful 140 d for a lie (ch_rollo_911_lied_franks). Sets ch_rollo_911_3.

cards.note: Step 4, the second turn: Rotomagus, before 911, forty days or more after Paris. The steward wants Frankish blades and horses. Real: the Edict of Pitres, 25 June 864, c. 25 (?): whoever gives or sells a byrnie, arms or a horse to the Northmen pays with his life (chronicle_793.json 864-06-25-pitres; dossiers/rotomagus.md 6); the king's fortified bridge at Pitres, 862 to 866 (Annales Bertiniani). The hanged cousin is invented. Payout: 250 d over the market for the iron (and a lasting cost: ch_rollo_911_armed, which the Franks remember and which closes the hard road of two endings), or a commission of wheat at a premium, or a true word on salt. Sets ch_rollo_911_4.

cards.note: Step 5, THE FORK: Rotomagus, from August 911 (to 913, so a late boat still meets it). Real: Rollo's army besieged Chartres and was beaten on 20 July 911 by Robert of Neustria and Richard of Burgundy; Bishop Gantelme showed the Virgin's tunic from the wall (Dudo, LATER; the day from the annals of Sainte-Colombe of Sens (?); a Saturday (?); realms/francia.md 'Chartres (20 July)'; Flodoard, Historia Remensis ecclesiae IV.14, for 'the war that Count Robert fought against them at Chartres'). That the camp was short of bread afterwards is ours, from what beaten armies did (892: the great army left Francia in a famine year, ASC). Needs only step 0 or 1, so steps 2 to 4 enrich the chain and never block it. Sets ch_rollo_911_5 and one road: ch_rollo_911_road_peace (with ch_rollo_911_fed), ch_rollo_911_road_church or ch_rollo_911_road_franks.

cards.note: Step 6 on the roads of peace and of the church: Rotomagus, two months after step 5. The meeting at Saint-Clair on the Epte, autumn 911: Rouen and the land to the sea granted to Rollo, who is to be baptised and to keep the river (Dudo of Saint-Quentin, about 1015, LATER, is the only teller; the grant itself is proved by King Charles's charter of 14 March 918; chronicle_793.json 911-rollo-rouen). The story of the king's foot is Dudo's and is told here as a story already going round, by a man who did not see it. The player waits with the boats at the river mouth: a merchant was not at the ford. Rollo is still unbaptised (faith old_gods). Sets ch_rollo_911_6.

cards.note: Step 6 on the road of the Franks, WHERE HISTORY CAN TURN: Parisius, twenty days after step 5. Count Robert himself asks. Real: the king's fortified bridge at Pitres (Pont-de-l'Arche), built 862 to 866 to bar the Seine (Annales Bertiniani), and taken in 885; that it could be timbered again in 911 is ours. Invented: that the grant hung on one boatman's count. In truth the king's counsellors had their way and Rollo got Rouen. Options: tell all (the Northmen are starved out; some drown at the bridge: ch_rollo_911_northmen_feud, a lasting cost); tell, and ask that those who leave are let go (ch_rollo_911_mercy: the hard and honest road); or think better of it and say they are strong, which puts the story back on the true road (ch_rollo_911_road_peace). Sets ch_rollo_911_6.

cards.note: Step 7, a turn: Rotomagus, from the spring of 912, four months after step 6. Real, by Dudo (c. 13, LATER; William of Jumieges ii follows him): Rollo baptised in 912 by the archbishop (Franco in Dudo), Robert of Neustria his sponsor, the name Robert; seven days in the white garments, each day a gift of land to a church (Saint Mary's of Rouen, of Bayeux, of Evreux, Saint Michael's in peril of the sea, Saint Peter's and Saint Ouen's at Rouen, Saint Peter's at Jumieges, Saint Denis's); on the eighth day he began to share out the land to his men by the rope. One article gives 915 for the baptism (dossiers/rotomagus.md 8). Men baptised more than once for the gift of a white garment: Notker, Gesta Karoli II.19, of Northmen at Louis the Pious's court, moved here as common talk. That the children already speak the Romance of Rouen: Dudo says William Longsword sent his son to Bayeux to learn the Danish tongue because Rouen spoke Romance (LATER). Payout: 150 d of wine sold, or Norse speech, or the count's and the archbishop's good will (ch_rollo_911_linen). Sets ch_rollo_911_7.

cards.note: Step 8: Rotomagus, from 913, two hundred days after the baptism. Rollo's law. Real, by Dudo c. 13 (LATER; retold, not quoted): theft forbidden, ploughs to be left in the field; the wife at Longpaon who hid her husband's plough irons; the five shillings; the ordeal of hot iron; both hanged, she for the theft and he for knowing. The gold rings hung on an oak by a pool and untouched for three years: William of Jumieges ii (dossiers/rotomagus.md 7). The net-maker and his boy are invented. The danger warns first (the steward's line). Each option is a fact; none only punishes: the court pays double or costs 10 d; fetching it back quietly pays in eels or costs 40 d; letting it go costs nothing and gives the Exeter Book's plough riddle. Sets ch_rollo_911_8.

cards.note: Step 9, and the last choice of road: Rotomagus, from 914. Real: Flodoard, Historia Remensis ecclesiae IV.14: after the war at Chartres the Northmen began to take the faith; Archbishop Herve of Reims (900 to 922), at the asking of the archbishop of Rouen (Wido, the lists' Witto), sent him twenty-three chapters gathered from the fathers on how such people should be handled, and asked Pope John (X, 914 to 928) what to do with men baptised and baptised again who lived as heathens, killed Christians and ate what had been offered to idols; the pope's answer was to go gently with the newly converted. So the letter is no earlier than 914. In 943 Turmod 'went back to idols and heathen rite' (Flodoard, Annales; dossiers/rotomagus.md 6). The newcomers and their goods are invented. Options: tell the steward (road_peace), carry the letter (road_church), or buy the plunder cheap (ch_rollo_911_bought_loot: keeps the road, closes both hard roads). Sets ch_rollo_911_9.

cards.note: ENDING 1, WHAT HAPPENED: Rotomagus, from 918. Flag ch_rollo_911_end_peace. Real: King Charles's charter of 14 March 918 for Saint-Germain-des-Pres excepts the part of an abbey's land 'which we granted to the Northmen of the Seine, namely Rollo and his companions, for the safeguarding of the kingdom' (our rendering; Recueil des actes de Charles III le Simple, ed. Lauer, no. 92 (?); spine cast.rollo); land shared by the rope (Dudo 13); the market that follows: about 1000 the men of Rouen pay toll at London on wine and whale (IV Aethelred 2; dossiers/rotomagus.md 4). Thorstein the shipmaster is invented (Old Norse Thorsteinn). Grand rewards: unlock_plot_rotomagus and unlock_charter_rotomagus with 900 d; or the HARD ROAD (fed the camp after Chartres, sold no iron, bought no plunder): those two and unlock_partner_thorstein with 1,400 d; or unlock_title_rollos_peace with 1,100 d and no land. Why a merchant could win them: Rollo gave land to those who had followed him, and a lord's spoken peace over a guest is the ordinary Norse way. If ch_rollo_911_armed is set the Franks up river remember (the steward says so).

cards.note: ENDING 2, WHAT HAPPENED, ON THE CHURCH'S SIDE: Rotomagus, from 918. Flag ch_rollo_911_end_saint. Real: the monks of Saint Peter's (Saint-Ouen) and the saint's body come back to Rouen in 918 (fr.wikipedia 'Abbaye Saint-Ouen de Rouen', 'Ouen de Rouen'; dossiers/rotomagus.md 2 and 5); the saint had been carried 'to Francia' in the raids (Dudo 13); Herve's twenty-three chapters and the pope's letter (Flodoard, Historia Remensis ecclesiae IV.14). That Rollo met the shrine at Longpaon and carried it is a later Rouen story (?): the card gives it as what the monks say. A cloth laid on a shrine and kept as a relic is the old custom of brandea (Gregory the Great, Epistolae IV.30). Grand rewards: unlock_title_st_ouens_man and unlock_plot_rotomagus (the abbey's cellar) with 800 d; or unlock_relic_st_ouen_cloth and the title with 600 d; or the HARD ROAD (no letter shown to the steward, no plunder bought): unlock_charter_rotomagus, the title and the relic with 1,200 d. Why a merchant could win them: abbeys had their own traders, freed of toll by charter (Saint-Germain-des-Pres, 779: dossiers/rotomagus.md 4).

cards.note: ENDING 3, HISTORY CHANGED: Parisius, four months after the bridge. Flags ch_rollo_911_end_river_shut and changed_rollo_911_no_grant. Nothing here happened: in truth the king granted Rouen and Rollo kept it. Built from what was real: the bridge at Pitres (Annales Bertiniani 862 to 866); armies that left a river when they could not eat (the great army crossing to Kent in 892, ASC); Robert's house holding Paris and the march. What follows in later years is in the chain page: no county of Rouen, no dukes, an archbishop's town with grass in its market, and the Seine open to the next fleet. Grand rewards: unlock_title_marquis_protection and unlock_charter_parisius with 1,200 d; or the HARD ROAD (asked mercy at the bridge and sold no iron): those two and unlock_pilot_seine with 1,500 d; or the title alone with 1,800 d. Why a merchant could win them: lords paid for news, and a count's hand over a trader and freedom from toll at one landing are what the charters of the time give (Saint-Germain-des-Pres, 779). Lasting cost: ch_rollo_911_northmen_feud, set at the bridge by the option 'all'.
